patients.label: 50-year-old male with chronic tinnitus treated with slow cortical potential neurofeedback training

identity_evidence.quote: A 50-year old male patient with tinnitus

attribution_limitations: The audiometry paragraph states a tested range of 0.125–16 kHz, but the methods list standard PTA frequencies from 0.25 kHz (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 kHz) and HFA frequencies from 9 kHz; the lowest tested frequency differs between the two statements.

The Fig. 3 caption says there were 5 days in blocks 2 and 3 (of possible 10), but Table 2 shows five value columns in block 2 and six in block 3 (days 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8); the Fig. 2 caption count of 7 days for blocks 2 and 3 matches Table 1.

Both figure captions give two alternative reasons for days without usable mean SCP amplitudes (the patient was not able or unable to participate or train, or the EEG was contaminated with artifacts) and do not say which applied to which day.

For the COGNITIVE, AUDITORY, RELAXATION and QUALITY OF LIFE subscales the printed after-training score is 0 but the printed percentage change (97.0, 96.2, 98.0 and 96.6 %) is not the 100 % that the printed footnote formula gives for a zero after-training score; the other subscale rows and the overall row agree with the formula.

In Tables 1 and 2 the Difference row cannot be exactly reproduced from the printed positive-trial and negative-trial values in 11 columns: most differ by 0.1 (for example Table 1 block 1 day 8, printed −4.6 and −19.6 with Difference 15.1), and in Table 2 block 1 day 5 and block 2 day 3 the printed Difference is positive although the positive-trial value is the lower one. The source does not state how the Difference row is calculated.
Table 5 prints the low beta change as "0.22 μV/17,6 %" with a decimal comma, while every other percentage in Tables 4 and 5 uses a decimal point.

The eyes-closed paragraph cites Fig. 6 (eyes closed) but Table 4 (eyes open) for a considerable drop of the high alpha amplitude at T3; both tables list a T3 high alpha decrease (Table 4: 1.54 to 0.9 μV; Table 5: 1.75 to 1.29 μV).

The text describes a similar, less pronounced delta reduction in the "right frontal areas" (Fig. 6; Table 5), while Table 5 prints "Right fronto-temporal" (electrode F8) for the right-sided delta row.
The text reports a 29 % change of the delta amplitude (eyes closed) while Table 5 prints 29.2 % for the matching row; the difference is rounding-level.
The authors say the patient reported "suppression of tinnitus sensation", while the results paragraph says tinnitus was still present and could be reduced by 20–30 %.

Table 4 row 1 prints the region "Temporo-occipital" without "Left" for electrodes F7, T3, T5 and O1, while Table 5 and the text give "Left temporo-occipital" for the same electrodes; the Table 5 header of the last column says "Percentage of change" although its cells print both an absolute difference and a percentage, as Table 4 states in its header.

limitations: Caption-layer visual_status stays not_inspected in this annotation; all seven figure JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.
Tables 1 and 2 print mean SCP amplitudes without a unit; a microvolt unit appears only inside the figure axes (pixels), so no unit is attached to those cells.

Dash cells in Tables 1 and 2 (training days without usable mean SCP amplitudes) are missing cells, not zero values, and are not recorded as facts; the captions give two alternative reasons and do not say which applied to which day.
Table 1 and 2 cell times are the Block and Day column headers; the day number is carried in the observation name because the Day header cells hold bare numerals.

Author interpretations and hypotheses (hedged TFI-based statements about sleep, optimism and cognitive clarity, mechanisms of the pitch change, why left-hemisphere effects were larger, cortical excitation threshold) are not extracted as patient facts; one hedged observation is kept review_only.

The introduction, the literature comparisons and the mechanistic discussion describe other studies and are background; discussion sentences that restate Tables 1 to 5 are merged into the matching table-cell facts instead of being repeated.

THI, BDI I and TFI were experimental Polish versions; the authors caution that interpretation thresholds of the original instruments may not transfer, and the interpretation words in the source are kept as the authors' wording.
Only the THI states a time ("before the training"); the baseline audiometry, BDI and HFA sentences state no time and are not given one.

Table 3 percentage cells, the Table 1 and 2 Difference rows, one decimal-comma cell, and several text-versus-table label differences are kept as printed and recorded as ambiguities; audiometry frequency range is recorded as a source conflict.
The patient's initials occur only inside verbatim evidence quotes; no authored field contains them.

evidence.quote: Finally, SCP Neurofeedback training was offered which the patient started at IPPH in 2013.
slow cortical potential (SCP) Neurofeedback training in chronic tinnitus
a series of specifically designed training sessions during which he practiced the self-regulation of SCPs

items.name: SCP Neurofeedback training

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: participated in three SCP training blocks, separated with 1-month breaks
The procedure comprised three 2-week training blocks.
The whole training period was approximately 3.5 months, with breaks of around 1 month in length between blocks
There were 3 training blocks (a maximum of 10 days each) separated by 1-month breaks.

items.name: SCP Neurofeedback training block schedule

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: Each block involved 10 × 1.5 h sessions from Monday to Friday.
we also applied smaller (25 %) number of transfer trials than feedback ones (75 %)
A single session consisted of 4 runs, each comprising 40 trials. There were 3 feedback and 1 transfer (with no feedback provided) runs performed in each session

items.name: SCP Neurofeedback session structure

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: During feedback runs each single trial was performed for 8 s.
If a low-frequency tone occurred, the patient was required to move consecutive red arrows upwards by producing cortical negativity (negative SCP trials) (see Fig. 1a).
Analogically, after hearing a high-frequency tone
was asked to move blue arrows downwards which corresponded with suppressing negativity or increasing positivity (positive SCP trials).

Whenever the patient produced the expected SCP shift, he also received a reward in a form of an attractive moving visual-auditory stimulus: a rotating sun animation, green light turning on and applause (Fig. 1a, left top corner).

items.name: SCP feedback runs

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: Red and blue arrows (pointing upwards and downwards, respectively) were shown on the training Visual Display (Fig. 1a).
He was also presented with either two high- or two low-frequency tones. The first and second tone marked the beginning and the end of a trial, respectively.
The arrows appeared every 0.5 s showing momentary amplitude values of the generated SCPs.
The amplitude of the SCP was calculated with reference to a 2 s pre-trial period.
In addition, the mean SCP amplitude value achieved during the whole trial was provided.
was asked to keep the track of the arrows.
was kept informed on his progress in the task.
Values below the arrows on the right side represent the mean amplitude of SCPs generated in a single trial.

items.name: SCP feedback display and amplitude reference

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: In the first session of block 1 the SCP amplitude threshold, which the patient had to exceed to be rewarded, was fixed to ensure the level of 30 % successful trials in each run. The value was set separately for positive and negative trials.

In subsequent sessions the thresholds were continuously updated, using mean SCP values obtained in all positive or negative SCP trials completed on the previous day, so that probability of success remained at approximately 30 %.
This approach yielded a stable difficulty levels throughout the whole training.

items.name: SCP reward threshold setting

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: In the first training block (block 1) the ratio of positive and negative SCP trials in the run was 1:1. In two remaining blocks (blocks 2 and 3), 66 % were positive SCP trials and 33 % were negative SCP trials (ratio 2:1).

The positive SCP and the negative SCP trials always came in a fixed order. In the training block 1 a positive SCP trial was always followed by a negative SCP trial. In blocks 2 and 3 after two positive SCP trials, a negative SCP trial was presented.
The fixed-order training schedule was applied to facilitate differentiation between the two types of trials.
The 2:1 ratio was set to accelerate the process of elevation of cortical excitation thresholds and, thereby, enhance cortical inhibitory mechanisms

Increasing number of positive trials was intentional since we want to facilitate increasing of the cortical excitation threshold hoping that it helps to attenuate the neuronal synchronization underlying tinnitus and alleviate tinnitus-related symptoms.

items.name: SCP positive-to-negative trial ratio and order

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: During transfer runs no feedback information was provided.
The sun animation and green diode were continuously presented on the Visual Display (Fig. 1b).

Whenever the mean SCP amplitude exceeded the threshold fixed at the level that predicted 30 % successful trials (see above), the sun animation rotated, the diode turned on and the applause sound was produced.

In each training block (1–3), transfer trials constituted the third run and were arranged in a fixed order. In block 1 the ratio of positive SCP trials to negative SCP trials was 1:1, whereas in blocks 2 and 3 the corresponding ratio became 2:1.

items.name: SCP transfer runs

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: also practiced self-regulation skills outside the IPPH. He was asked to sit in front of a PC and use a printed Visual Display of the training procedure, imaging an actual training session at the Institute.
during which the patient was encouraged to train at home without using the Neurofeedback equipment

items.name: Home practice of SCP self-regulation

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: The EEG signal used for Neurofeedback was registered from the active electrode placed at the vertex (Cz position) (Jasper ). Reference electrodes were located on linked mastoids and the ground electrode was placed on the back of the neck (C7 position).
The EEG signal recorded in each training session was carefully inspected offline and grand average SCP was calculated based only on artefact-free trials.

items.name: EEG recording during SCP Neurofeedback training

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: During the training, electro-oculogram (EOG) was recorded from two additional electrodes attached above and below the right eye
The EOG signal was used by the instructor and by the patient himself to monitor and reduce the effect of eye movements on the amplitude of the produced SCPs.
The patient was also asked to refrain from eye movements during positive and negative SCP trials and try to blink only during 2-min breaks between them.

If eye movements during an SCP trial were too intensive, a red alarm control light turned on in the top left corner of the patient’s training screen suggesting him to stop blinking (Fig. 1a, b). This trial was considered failed due to the eye movement-related artefacts, even if the required SCP amplitude threshold was obtained, and the patient did not receive the reward

evidence.quote: The following diagnostic tests: (a) standard and high-frequency pure tone audiometry (0.125–16 kHz), (b) Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) (Newman et al. ) and Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) (Beck et al. ) were administered to the patient.

A standard and a high-frequency pure tone audiometry (PTA and HFA, respectively) were performed by an expert audiologist in a sound-proof chamber according to ISO 8253-1 () standards and recommendations by the British Society of Audiology ().
All measurements were performed with the use of a Madsen Astera audiometer (GN Otometrics, Germany) and Sennheiser HDA-200 headphones
Both tests were performed according to a modified ascending Hughson–Westlake procedure

The task of the patient was to press a special button when a tone was heard. If the patient was able to detect the tone, the sound level was reduced by 10 dB; if not, the sound level was increased by 5 dB. This procedure was repeated several times, until a 50 % response rate was obtained for a given level of the test signal and until hearing thresholds for all tested frequencies were determined.

evidence.quote: The patient was first asked to describe the sound of tinnitus in his own words (e.g. a tone, hiss, noise, etc.), and to estimate its loudness and laterality. Then the Tinnitus software was used.

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: The patient was seated in a comfortable reclining armchair and was asked to relax. In the first block the patient kept his eyes open and fixated on a point of his choice in the room. In the second block his eyes were closed.
The signal was referenced to linked mastoids and the ground electrode was placed in the FCz position.

items.name: QEEG recording conditions (eyes open and eyes closed)

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: The registered signal was then analysed quantitatively using WinEEG software (Mitsar Co. Ltd.). Digital pre-processing involved high- and low-pass filtering within the range of 0.5–50 Hz.
Next, the artefact-free EEG signal was divided into thirty 4.096 s segments and the spectral analysis was performed using the fast Fourier transform (FFT)

Further quantitative analysis involved the following frequency bands: delta (1–4 Hz), theta (4–8 Hz), low alpha (8–10 Hz), high alpha (10–12 Hz), low beta (12–15 Hz), middle beta (15–18 Hz), and high beta (18–25 Hz).

evidence.quote: Delta (1–4 Hz) [rowspan=2,colspan=1] | Left fronto-temporalLeft temporalTemporo-occipitalLeft occipital | F7, T3, T5, O1 | 1.85 | 1.18 | ↓ | 0.67 μV/36.2 %
Frequency band | Brain regions | Electrodes | Before training (μV) | After training (μV) | Direction of change | Absolute difference (μV)/percentage change

Mean absolute amplitudes of specific frequency bands, estimated from QEEG signals registered before and after SCP Neurofeedback training in the eyes open condition at electrodes revealing most significant effects.

After training, the QEEG analysis demonstrated reduced mean absolute amplitude of the delta frequency band (1–4 Hz) in the left fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital and occipital brain regions (Fig. 4).
The effect was visible at electrodes F7, T3, T5 and O1 and most apparent for 1.46 Hz in the left temporo-occipital and occipital areas (Fig. 5, Table 4).

A comparative QEEG analysis of signals recorded before and after treatment showed that delta and theta band mean absolute amplitudes were reduced both in signals recorded in the eyes open and the eyes closed conditions (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).

The most significant amplitude reductions were indicated in fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital (delta and theta) and occipital (delta) regions in the left hemisphere (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).

Mean absolute amplitudes of specific frequency bands, estimated from QEEG signals registered before and after SCP Neurofeedback training in the eyes closed condition at electrodes revealing most significant effects.

The QEEG analysis revealed delta band (1–4 Hz) as the one whose amplitude was mostly affected by the SCP Neurofeedback training (29 % change in the amplitude). The effect was most visible at electrodes F7, T3, T5 and O1 in the left fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital and occipital brain regions (Figs. 6, 7; Table 5).

A comparative QEEG analysis of signals recorded before and after treatment showed that delta and theta band mean absolute amplitudes were reduced both in signals recorded in the eyes open and the eyes closed conditions (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).

The most significant amplitude reductions were indicated in fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital (delta and theta) and occipital (delta) regions in the left hemisphere (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).

claims.text: A 50-year-old male patient had suffered from chronic tinnitus since 2006, a loud sound in both ears and/or inside the head that became a chronic high-frequency squeak, extremely bothersome, impeding falling asleep and more intensive under stress. Methods tried over the next 3 years, including tinnitus retraining therapy, were ineffective; he lost his job and did not accept prescribed sedative and SSRI medication.

There were 3 training blocks (a maximum of 10 days each) separated by 1-month breaks.

we also applied smaller (25 %) number of transfer trials than feedback ones (75 %)
A single session consisted of 4 runs, each comprising 40 trials. There were 3 feedback and 1 transfer (with no feedback provided) runs performed in each session

In the first training block (block 1) the ratio of positive and negative SCP trials in the run was 1:1. In two remaining blocks (blocks 2 and 3), 66 % were positive SCP trials and 33 % were negative SCP trials (ratio 2:1).

The positive SCP and the negative SCP trials always came in a fixed order. In the training block 1 a positive SCP trial was always followed by a negative SCP trial. In blocks 2 and 3 after two positive SCP trials, a negative SCP trial was presented.
The fixed-order training schedule was applied to facilitate differentiation between the two types of trials.
The 2:1 ratio was set to accelerate the process of elevation of cortical excitation thresholds and, thereby, enhance cortical inhibitory mechanisms

Increasing number of positive trials was intentional since we want to facilitate increasing of the cortical excitation threshold hoping that it helps to attenuate the neuronal synchronization underlying tinnitus and alleviate tinnitus-related symptoms.
During transfer runs no feedback information was provided.

claims.text: After the training tinnitus was still present, but the patient reported lower pitch and loudness, better sleep, more control and improved daily life. Matched tinnitus pitch fell to 11 kHz and intensity to 30 dB HL, and the overall TFI score fell from 45 to 6 points. QEEG showed decreased delta, theta and alpha amplitudes in left-hemisphere regions and increased high beta amplitude at T6 and T3 in the eyes-open recording.

evidence.quote: After SCP Neurofeedback training Z.C. reported that tinnitus was still present.
After the training the patient reported decreased tinnitus loudness and pitch, as well as improved quality of daily life.
He stated, however, that the pitch of tinnitus decreased and the sensation became less intensive.
In addition, his sleep quality improved and it was easier to fall asleep and get up more rested.
The interview revealed that the most important benefit for the patient was that he felt in control of the tinnitus sensation and was able to reduce it by 20–30 %.

As stated by the patient during a clinical interview, after the training the severity of tinnitus alleviated, the sensation became more controllable and affected the life of the patient to a lesser extent.
considerable improvement of quality of daily life
substantial improvement in various aspects of everyday life
After the training, the perceived pitch of tinnitus was reduced to 11 kHz and the intensity decreased to 30 dB HL.
In the present study not only did the loudness but also the pitch of the patient’s tinnitus decrease following SCP Neurofeedback therapy.

After training, the QEEG analysis demonstrated reduced mean absolute amplitude of the delta frequency band (1–4 Hz) in the left fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital and occipital brain regions (Fig. 4).
The effect was visible at electrodes F7, T3, T5 and O1 and most apparent for 1.46 Hz in the left temporo-occipital and occipital areas (Fig. 5, Table 4).

A comparative QEEG analysis of signals recorded before and after treatment showed that delta and theta band mean absolute amplitudes were reduced both in signals recorded in the eyes open and the eyes closed conditions (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).

The most significant amplitude reductions were indicated in fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital (delta and theta) and occipital (delta) regions in the left hemisphere (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).

limitations: Caption-layer visual_status stays not_inspected in this annotation; all seven figure JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.
Tables 1 and 2 print mean SCP amplitudes without a unit; a microvolt unit appears only inside the figure axes (pixels), so no unit is attached to those cells.

Dash cells in Tables 1 and 2 (training days without usable mean SCP amplitudes) are missing cells, not zero values, and are not recorded as facts; the captions give two alternative reasons and do not say which applied to which day.
Table 1 and 2 cell times are the Block and Day column headers; the day number is carried in the observation name because the Day header cells hold bare numerals.

Author interpretations and hypotheses (hedged TFI-based statements about sleep, optimism and cognitive clarity, mechanisms of the pitch change, why left-hemisphere effects were larger, cortical excitation threshold) are not extracted as patient facts; one hedged observation is kept review_only.

The introduction, the literature comparisons and the mechanistic discussion describe other studies and are background; discussion sentences that restate Tables 1 to 5 are merged into the matching table-cell facts instead of being repeated.

THI, BDI I and TFI were experimental Polish versions; the authors caution that interpretation thresholds of the original instruments may not transfer, and the interpretation words in the source are kept as the authors' wording.
Only the THI states a time ("before the training"); the baseline audiometry, BDI and HFA sentences state no time and are not given one.

slow cortical potential (SCP) Neurofeedback training in chronic tinnitus
a series of specifically designed training sessions during which he practiced the self-regulation of SCPs
participated in three SCP training blocks, separated with 1-month breaks
The procedure comprised three 2-week training blocks.
The whole training period was approximately 3.5 months, with breaks of around 1 month in length between blocks
There were 3 training blocks (a maximum of 10 days each) separated by 1-month breaks.
Each block involved 10 × 1.5 h sessions from Monday to Friday.
we also applied smaller (25 %) number of transfer trials than feedback ones (75 %)
A single session consisted of 4 runs, each comprising 40 trials. There were 3 feedback and 1 transfer (with no feedback provided) runs performed in each session
During feedback runs each single trial was performed for 8 s.
If a low-frequency tone occurred, the patient was required to move consecutive red arrows upwards by producing cortical negativity (negative SCP trials) (see Fig. 1a).
Analogically, after hearing a high-frequency tone
was asked to move blue arrows downwards which corresponded with suppressing negativity or increasing positivity (positive SCP trials).

Whenever the patient produced the expected SCP shift, he also received a reward in a form of an attractive moving visual-auditory stimulus: a rotating sun animation, green light turning on and applause (Fig. 1a, left top corner).

In the first session of block 1 the SCP amplitude threshold, which the patient had to exceed to be rewarded, was fixed to ensure the level of 30 % successful trials in each run. The value was set separately for positive and negative trials.

In subsequent sessions the thresholds were continuously updated, using mean SCP values obtained in all positive or negative SCP trials completed on the previous day, so that probability of success remained at approximately 30 %.
This approach yielded a stable difficulty levels throughout the whole training.

In the first training block (block 1) the ratio of positive and negative SCP trials in the run was 1:1. In two remaining blocks (blocks 2 and 3), 66 % were positive SCP trials and 33 % were negative SCP trials (ratio 2:1).

The positive SCP and the negative SCP trials always came in a fixed order. In the training block 1 a positive SCP trial was always followed by a negative SCP trial. In blocks 2 and 3 after two positive SCP trials, a negative SCP trial was presented.
The fixed-order training schedule was applied to facilitate differentiation between the two types of trials.
The 2:1 ratio was set to accelerate the process of elevation of cortical excitation thresholds and, thereby, enhance cortical inhibitory mechanisms

Increasing number of positive trials was intentional since we want to facilitate increasing of the cortical excitation threshold hoping that it helps to attenuate the neuronal synchronization underlying tinnitus and alleviate tinnitus-related symptoms.

In each training block (1–3), transfer trials constituted the third run and were arranged in a fixed order. In block 1 the ratio of positive SCP trials to negative SCP trials was 1:1, whereas in blocks 2 and 3 the corresponding ratio became 2:1.

The EEG signal used for Neurofeedback was registered from the active electrode placed at the vertex (Cz position) (Jasper ). Reference electrodes were located on linked mastoids and the ground electrode was placed on the back of the neck (C7 position).
The EEG signal recorded in each training session was carefully inspected offline and grand average SCP was calculated based only on artefact-free trials.
During the training, electro-oculogram (EOG) was recorded from two additional electrodes attached above and below the right eye
The EOG signal was used by the instructor and by the patient himself to monitor and reduce the effect of eye movements on the amplitude of the produced SCPs.
The patient was also asked to refrain from eye movements during positive and negative SCP trials and try to blink only during 2-min breaks between them.

If eye movements during an SCP trial were too intensive, a red alarm control light turned on in the top left corner of the patient’s training screen suggesting him to stop blinking (Fig. 1a, b). This trial was considered failed due to the eye movement-related artefacts, even if the required SCP amplitude threshold was obtained, and the patient did not receive the reward

evidence.quote: In the first training block (block 1) the ratio of positive and negative SCP trials in the run was 1:1. In two remaining blocks (blocks 2 and 3), 66 % were positive SCP trials and 33 % were negative SCP trials (ratio 2:1).

The positive SCP and the negative SCP trials always came in a fixed order. In the training block 1 a positive SCP trial was always followed by a negative SCP trial. In blocks 2 and 3 after two positive SCP trials, a negative SCP trial was presented.
The fixed-order training schedule was applied to facilitate differentiation between the two types of trials.
The 2:1 ratio was set to accelerate the process of elevation of cortical excitation thresholds and, thereby, enhance cortical inhibitory mechanisms

Increasing number of positive trials was intentional since we want to facilitate increasing of the cortical excitation threshold hoping that it helps to attenuate the neuronal synchronization underlying tinnitus and alleviate tinnitus-related symptoms.

Mean absolute amplitudes of specific frequency bands, estimated from QEEG signals registered before and after SCP Neurofeedback training in the eyes open condition at electrodes revealing most significant effects.

After training, the QEEG analysis demonstrated reduced mean absolute amplitude of the delta frequency band (1–4 Hz) in the left fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital and occipital brain regions (Fig. 4).
The effect was visible at electrodes F7, T3, T5 and O1 and most apparent for 1.46 Hz in the left temporo-occipital and occipital areas (Fig. 5, Table 4).

A comparative QEEG analysis of signals recorded before and after treatment showed that delta and theta band mean absolute amplitudes were reduced both in signals recorded in the eyes open and the eyes closed conditions (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).

The most significant amplitude reductions were indicated in fronto-temporal, temporal, temporo-occipital (delta and theta) and occipital (delta) regions in the left hemisphere (Figs. 4, 5, 6 and 7; Tables 4, 5).
